solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruby anniversary, out to save relationship!

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to go forth is to go out
a tie is a bond or relationship between people

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a couple going out to celebrate their ruby wedding and keep their marriage alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby wedding marks forty years of marriage, so the ruby anniversary is the one numbered forty in the sequence.

clue.text: Sword with Nazi inscription, museum piece

indicators.note: an inscription is written into an object, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a foil is a fencing sword
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A sword engraved with Nazi lettering on display in a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified ancient remains are exhibits in museums; figuratively it also means an old-fashioned thing.

clue.text: Tell part of the tale, rather uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a section of a fairly upbeat story.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Tell part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the hiding indicator; 'Tell' alone is the definition. In a down clue 'uplifting' reads ETALER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to recount or narrate a story to someone.

clue.text: Love throwing chap up into air too carelessly

indicators.note: into says the turned piece goes inside the rearranged letters
carelessly means done without order, so these letters are rearranged
throwing up, in a down clue, means lifting the word so it reads bottom to top
up in a down clue means read from the bottom, the word turned round

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A lover carelessly tosses a man into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' here is a noun for a beloved person, not the feeling; 'throwing ... up' is split around the chap, and up suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, the one called my love, a term of address for a beloved.

clue.text: Creature hiding underground: with predator, drop is perilous

indicators.note: something perilous is unstable, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal lies in wait: with a predator about, a fall is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid lives in a burrow sealed with a hinged lid, lurking underground to ambush prey.

clue.text: One of two lines read initially, in matter for discussion

indicators.note: in says the first piece is placed inside the discussion matter

parts.note: a topic is a subject or matter for discussion

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of read is used

explanation.surface: Someone reads the first of two lines aloud to set up a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are the two lines of latitude bounding the torrid zone, so each is one of a pair.

clue.text: Just ceremony to be broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Asking whether a ceremony is worth televising.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean fair or morally correct.

clue.text: Fielder bats after Pakistani opener taken

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the first piece
opener means the first letter of the next word
bats is slang for crazy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fielder comes in to bat once the Pakistani opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' and 'opener' look like cricket; 'bats' signals the anagram and 'opener' takes P.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles meaning stolen, especially in petty amounts.

clue.text: Most vulgar actress wildly embracing love

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other
wildly means in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: The crudest actress throws her arms around her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are superlatives meaning crudest or most lacking refinement.

clue.text: Business adviser gives one a nosebleed, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a consultant called in to fix problems in a firm
hooter is British slang for the nose, so it gives the nose trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word after TROUBLES; hooter is British slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant hired to identify and resolve problems in an organisation is given this title.

clue.text: Royal fruit

definitions.meaning: a sultan's wife, mother or daughter is a royal personage
a dried seedless grape used in baking

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sultan's consort, a royal lady, and a pale dried grape used in cakes.

clue.text: One for the road possibly knocked back in the Crown and Sceptre?

indicators.note: in says the numeral for one is set within the reversed drink
knocked back says the drink's letters are turned round, as a drink is downed

parts.note: a drink one for the road might be a lager
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A last drink downed at a pub called the Crown and Sceptre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reverses A LAGER to REGALA; 'in' puts I inside it. The Crown and Sceptre looks like a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown and sceptre are examples of the ceremonial emblems of monarchy, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Opener interested in bagging runs

indicators.note: bagging means catching and holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to be into something is to be interested in it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket opener keen on scoring runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or a talk, the part that starts it.

clue.text: Oldest bus in need of repair, of course

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The oldest bus in the fleet obviously needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions are adverbs of certainty, meaning surely or without question.

clue.text: Academic postman?

definitions.meaning: playfully, a man who handles letters all day

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'letters' as mail rather than learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly writer is called this, and a postman is literally a male carrier of mail.

clue.text: Rated awful, factory routine

indicators.note: awful means badly made, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: A factory's work routine has been rated as dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a monotonous, wearisome round of work is called this, after the exercise machine.

clue.text: In parts, classic screening is old and dreary, primarily

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind cover, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: an epic is a great classic work

indicators.note: primarily says the first letters of the words are used

explanation.surface: A review: a classic film being screened is old and dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In parts' is the definition, an adjectival phrase for something told in instalments; 'screening' looks like film showing but signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic comes in separate instalments, so it is presented in parts.

clue.text: Oddly, nana wears crown for party

indicators.note: wears means has on, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the crown of something is its height or highest point

indicators.note: oddly says take the first, third and further odd letters

explanation.surface: Grandma, unusually, dons a crown to go partying.
explanation.walkthrough: A HEN NIGHT is a British party for a bride-to-be and her friends before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration, a kind of party held before a woman's wedding.

clue.text: Worried piano will get taken back

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
goods taken back by a creditor are repossessed

explanation.surface: Someone frets that their piano will be seized by the bailiffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prepossessed is to be preoccupied, the mind already taken up by a concern.

clue.text: Reddish-brown char, gold on top

indicators.note: on top in a down clue says the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to char is to burn

explanation.surface: A description of a scorched colour with a golden sheen above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown colour, usually said of hair.

clue.text: Numbers still wearing smalls

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: S is small, so smalls is two of them
even means still, as in even more

explanation.surface: Some figures still dressed in their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: SMALLS is British slang for underwear, here two S abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens are examples of numbers, the figure 7.

clue.text: Southern Iran and Oman formed another country

indicators.note: formed means made into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Southern Iran and Oman joined up to make a new nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny republic enclosed by Italy, it is a country distinct from the two named in the clue.

clue.text: A confusing network, wow!

parts.note: a maze is a confusing network of paths

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a puzzling network.
explanation.definitionFit: Both say to astonish; the exclamation in the clue is an imperative telling someone to impress.

clue.text: Level of tennis where vitality under discussion?

indicators.note: under discussion means being spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: juice is slang for energy or vitality

explanation.surface: A question about the stage of a tennis match where players' energy is being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The likeness relies on a common British pronunciation where the opening of the scoring word sounds like J.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this is the score when both players reach forty, leaving the game level.

clue.text: Shame qualification not entirely inspiring Bill

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside
not entirely says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a degree is an academic qualification
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: Bill, it seems, finds it a disgrace that he never quite finished his degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to humiliate or bring dishonour upon someone.

clue.text: Champion, one of twenty-four in harmony

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: to be in tune is to be in harmony
a human has twenty-four ribs, twelve pairs

explanation.surface: A champion singer, one of twenty-four in a choir singing in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune was a Roman official who defended the people, so the word means a champion of popular rights.

clue.text: Ship heading for Cornwall, say

indicators.note: heading for means the head, or first letter, of the next word

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A vessel sails toward Cornwall, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' looks like travel; it picks the C of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small single-masted sailing vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Sweets — fifty in Persian confection

indicators.note: in says the fifty numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
a confection is something mixed together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty sugary treats in a Persian dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confection' looks like part of the dessert picture but signals the rearrangement of PERSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: These are nut-and-caramelised-sugar confectionery, so they are sweets.
